title: Design System: حكايات مصرية / Egyptian Stories

masthead.purpose: The magazine title on the contents page, struck twice off-register. Never reused for content.

numeral.purpose: The reader's page number, in Arabic-Indic digits.

plate-title-ar.purpose: Grid plate titles and knocked-out press blocks.

story-ar.purpose: Long reading text in Noto Naskh, 44px leading on 23px.

story-en.purpose: The English track and the second-pass crib.

stamp.purpose: All apparatus labels: letter-spaced Archivo caps, always uppercased.

shadows.name: laid-plate
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. A sheet of stock sitting on the press bed. Never applied to stamps, rules, icons or bands.

motion.name: plate-lay-down
motion.purpose: The authored moment: a fresh plate settling from 26px off-spine, 14px down and 1.4deg off-square into position. Mirrors with text direction.

motion.name: art-drift
motion.purpose: Slow scale-and-pan (1.14 to 1.3, ±30px x, ±18px y) on illustrations only. Bounded at 3 iterations so the page comes to rest.

motion.name: plate-press
motion.purpose: Pressed feedback on a tappable plate.

keylines.name: hair
keylines.purpose: Stamps, filter stamps, pips, internal dividers.

keylines.name: keyline
keylines.purpose: Printed rules, press block frames, turn buttons.

keylines.name: heavy
keylines.purpose: Plate borders, masthead rule, the line under an illustration block.

target.name: minimum-interactive-height
target.purpose: The audience starts at two years old. Square cut grows a minHeight rather than softening into a pill.

components.name: Plate
components.description: A sheet of stock laid on the press ground: halftone, heavy keyline, and the system's only shadow.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-plate { position: relative; background: #F5ECD8; border: 3.5px solid #17120F; border-radius: 0; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 3px 5px 10px rgba(18,7,4,0.42); width: 280px; direction: rtl; background-image: radial-gradient(#17120F 1.15px, transparent 1.15px); background-size: 6px 6px; } .ds-plate-block { aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; background: #1B4D9B; border-bottom: 3.5px solid #17120F; } .ds-plate-body { padding: 10px; } .ds-plate-title { font-family: Lalezar, sans-serif; font-size: 30px; line-height: 42px; color: #17120F; margin: 0; text-align: right; } .ds-plate-title-en { font-family: Lalezar, sans-serif; font-size: 21px; line-height: 27px; color: #241B15; margin: 2px 0 0; text-align: right; } .ds-plate-stamps { display: flex; gap: 6px; margin-top: 6px; } .ds-plate-origin { font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 1.1px; font-weight: 600; color: #6E5A48; margin: 6px 0 0; text-align: right; }

components.name: Stamp
components.description: The apparatus of a printed issue: age band, running time, provenance. Square keyline, letter-spaced caps.
components.css: .ds-stamp { display: inline-block; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 1.1px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; color: #17120F; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #17120F; border-radius: 0; padding: 2px 6px; } .ds-stamp-filled { background: #17120F; color: #F5ECD8; }

components.name: Filter Stamp
components.description: The stamp language grown to a 46px touch target, printed straight onto the press ground. Selected state flips the fill.
components.css: .ds-filterbar { display: flex; gap: 6px; background: #C8321E; padding: 12px; direction: rtl; } .ds-filter-stamp { font-family: NotoNaskhArabic, serif; font-size: 12px; color: #FBF3E2; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #FBF3E2; border-radius: 0; padding: 0 16px; min-height: 46px; min-width: 46px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-filter-stamp:hover { background: rgba(251,243,226,0.14); } .ds-filter-stamp:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F2B01E; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-filter-stamp-active { background: #FBF3E2; color: #C8321E; }

components.name: Turn Button
components.description: The reader's page-turn control. Square, 2px keyline, chevron facing computed from render-time layout direction.
components.html: <button class="ds-turn" aria-label="Next page"><svg width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none"><path d="M15 4 L7 12 L15 20" stroke="#FBF3E2" stroke-width="2.4" fill="none"/></svg></button><button class="ds-turn" disabled aria-label="Previous page"><svg width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none"><path d="M9 4 L17 12 L9 20" stroke="#FBF3E2" stroke-width="2.4" fill="none"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-turn { background: transparent; border: 2px solid #FBF3E2; border-radius: 0; padding: 0 24px; min-height: 46px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; cursor: pointer; margin-left: 8px; } .ds-turn:hover { background: rgba(168,39,21,0.5); } .ds-turn:active { background: #A82715; } .ds-turn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F2B01E; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-turn[disabled] { opacity: 0.32; cursor: default; }

components.name: Masthead
components.description: The contents page band: deeper ground run, halftone, title struck twice off-register, heavy rule, and a two-edge caps foot.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-masthead { position: relative; background: #A82715; padding: 10px 16px; direction: rtl; overflow: hidden; background-image: radial-gradient(#17120F 1.15px, transparent 1.15px); background-size: 5px 5px; } .ds-masthead-title { position: relative; font-family: Lalezar, sans-serif; font-size: 52px; line-height: 58px; } .ds-masthead-offset { position: absolute; inset: 0; color: #F2B01E; transform: translate(2px, 2px); } .ds-masthead-black { position: relative; color: #FBF3E2; } .ds-masthead-rule { height: 3.5px; background: #FBF3E2; margin-top: 6px; } .ds-masthead-foot { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin-top: 6px; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 1.1px; font-weight: 700; color: #FBF3E2; }

components.name: Press Block
components.description: The block a magazine prints when the engraver has not delivered a picture. Nine of ten stories render this, so it is the most-seen surface in the app.
components.html: جحا والحمار
components.css: .ds-pressblock { position: relative; background: #17120F; aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; width: 260px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background-image: radial-gradient(rgba(245,236,216,0.2) 1.15px, transparent 1.15px); background-size: 4px 4px; } .ds-pressblock-frame { margin: 16px; border: 2px solid #F5ECD8; padding: 16px 10px; width: 100%; } .ds-pressblock-title { display: block; font-family: Lalezar, sans-serif; font-size: 30px; line-height: 42px; color: #F5ECD8; text-align: center; direction: rtl; } .ds-pressblock-lozenge { position: absolute; top: 6px; right: 6px; }

components.name: Page Pips
components.description: The reader's page indicator: square 9px pips, hairline keyline, solid fill on the current page.
components.css: .ds-pips { display: flex; gap: 6px; background: #C8321E; padding: 10px; } .ds-pip { width: 9px; height: 9px; border: 1px solid #FBF3E2; border-radius: 0; } .ds-pip-on { background: #FBF3E2; }

components.name: Second Pass Toggle
components.description: Lays the English impression under the Arabic one. Authored two-sheets icon, never a globe or a flag.
components.css: .ds-secondpass { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; background: transparent; color: #FBF3E2; border: 1px solid #FBF3E2; border-radius: 0; padding: 0 16px; min-height: 46px; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 1.1px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; } .ds-secondpass:hover { background: rgba(251,243,226,0.14); } .ds-secondpass:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F2B01E; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-secondpass[aria-pressed="true"] { background: #FBF3E2; color: #C8321E; }

narrative.overview:
This is a Cairo children's magazine of the 1960s-80s — Samir, Mickey — printed in a handful of spot inks on cheap paper, with visible halftone and sloppy registration. The screen is the press bed, not a page: the ink owns the ground, and paper only ever appears as plates laid on top of it, edged in a heavy keyline and carrying a real cast shadow. Two worlds are refused by name: the rounded-card kids' app with its pills and bubbles, and its opposite, the cream-and-pastel bedtime minimal.

Density is editorial rather than airy. Material separates with printed ink — rules, keylines, halftone, letter-spaced caps — before it separates with whitespace. Every surface sits under a faint dot screen (~10% opacity, 4-7px pitch) that is findable when you look for it and invisible while reading. Display type is struck twice, a coloured impression laid down first and the black struck over it two pixels off-register, which is the one detail that makes cheap colour printing unmistakable.

Two registers exist, and night is not day dimmed. The press changes inks: the ground goes from press vermilion to oxblood, paper plates become kraft board, and paper white never appears after dark. Arabic leads throughout — the whole surface hangs from the right spine regardless of which language track the reader selects.
keyCharacteristics: Committed colour: press ink owns roughly a third of every screen; paper is a laid object, never the field.
Square cuts only — zero radius anywhere in the build.
Misregistration by 2px on display type, as a device, not an accident.
Two ink registers (day / night), not one palette at two brightnesses.
RTL as structure, Arabic-Indic numerals as default.

rules.name: The Committed Ground Rule
rules.body: The press ink owns the screen. Paper never becomes the background; it appears only as a plate laid on the ink, edged in a heavy keyline. A cream page with coloured trim is the default this world exists to refuse.

rules.name: The Changed Ink Rule
rules.body: Night is a different press run, not a dimmer. The ground moves to oxblood, plates move to kraft board, and paper white never appears at night — a sheet of white paper in a dark bedroom is a defect.

rules.name: The Overprint Rule
rules.body: Artwork rendered at night is overprinted with the press ground at 0.34 opacity, so a daylight image is never the brightest object on a bedtime screen.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Lalezar is the only display face, day and night, Arabic and Latin. Reading text never uses it, and no second display face is ever introduced.

rules.name: The Second Impression Rule
rules.body: Display titles print in two passes: a coloured ink laid down first, the black struck over it by misregister (2px; 2.5px on the lead plate). The offset pass is hidden from assistive technology — only the black pass carries the string.

rules.name: The Arabic Numeral Rule
rules.body: Counts, ages and page numbers set in Arabic-Indic digits (٠١٢٣…). Latin digits are the tell of a layout built for English and translated afterwards.

rules.name: The Right Spine Rule
rules.body: The page is laid out right-to-left always, regardless of the selected language track — Arabic leads, so the whole surface hangs from the right spine, not just the Arabic text nodes. Direction must be read at render time (isRTL()), never captured at module load, and on web the document's dir must be consulted because react-native-web's I18nManager.isRTL lies.

rules.name: The Minimum Target Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element carries a minimum height of 46px (TARGET). The audience starts at two years old; the square cut keeps its shape and grows a minHeight rather than softening into a larger pill.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: Only plates cast shadows. Stamps, rules, icons, filters and the masthead are flat against the ground; giving any of them elevation turns the press bed into a UI surface.

rules.name: The Halftone Rule
rules.body: Every printed surface sits under the dot screen — the ground at 7px pitch, the masthead at 5px, plates at the theme default (6px), press blocks opened up to 4-5px at 0.2 opacity. The dot is drawn as a real SVG pattern, never a bitmap tile.

dos: Do let the press ink own the ground and put paper on it as a plate with a 3.5px keyline.
Do keep every corner square (0px radius) and let keyline weight carry the hierarchy (1 / 2 / 3.5px).
Do put the halftone screen under every printed surface.
Do strike display titles twice, the coloured impression 2px off-register under the black, and hide the offset pass from assistive tech.
Do set counts, ages and page numbers in Arabic-Indic digits.
Do lay out right-to-left always, and read direction at render time via isRTL().
Do give every interactive element a 46px minimum height without softening its shape.
Do change inks for night — oxblood ground, kraft board plates — and overprint artwork at 0.34.
Do draw new icons in the family: 2.4 stroke, butt caps, mitre joins, authored paths.
donts: Don't make paper the background or the ground a trim colour.
Don't use rounded corners, pills, or capsule chips anywhere.
Don't print vermilion as a plate ink — it owns the ground and would disappear on it.
Don't use white, or any paper-value light, at night.
Don't add a second display face, or set reading text in Lalezar.
Don't add shadows to anything but plates; separate with ink, not with elevation.
Don't use emoji, icon fonts, or imported icon-set glyphs.
Don't let motion run unbounded — the drift stops after 3 iterations and the plate comes to rest.
Don't let the reading column exceed its measure (560px, 1040px on a spread) by growing plates to fill a desktop window.
